strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Prevents headless selected-candidate continuations from starting from registry evidence that points back to the already-active remote Mode Pack.
Makes registry update selection compare active and candidate identity in the same domain instead of comparing candidate content SHA-256 to activation fingerprint.
Fails closed before selection evidence is committed when the candidate identity matches the active Mode Pack.
Preserves bounded selection ledger evidence by recording no ModePackRegistryUpdateSelected event for same-active candidates.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: modepack.selectRegistryUpdate rejects a registry candidate that matches the active remote Mode Pack identity before creating selected-candidate evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The prior guard compared candidate_content_sha256 to current activation_fingerprint, which are different fingerprint domains and can miss already-active candidates.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless update continuations could fetch, verify, approve, or replace a candidate that is not a real update because it already matches the active Mode Pack.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M46.1 fetched selected candidates, M46.2 verified selected candidate provenance, and R6.1 bound continuation replay identity; R6.2 changes registry selection admission before continuation evidence exists.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing modepack.selectRegistryUpdate behavior changes; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. Existing bounded error behavior and absence of selection ledger evidence are sufficient.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust runtime denies same-active registry candidates with same-domain identity comparison before ModePackRegistryUpdateSelected evidence is persisted.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers cannot build selected-candidate continuation chains from already-active registry candidates.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the known R6 selection-integrity blocker left after R6.1 before M46.3 approval continuation resumes.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: R6.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and archives the R6.2 value gate. Review must confirm this is runtime selection admission behavior, not a report or readiness wrapper.

exit_criteria: modepack.selectRegistryUpdate denies registry entries whose candidate identity matches the currently active remote Mode Pack using same-domain active/candidate identity semantics.
The denial is proven when candidate_content_sha256 and current activation_fingerprint differ, demonstrating the prior predicate would not have denied the candidate.
Denied same-active selection persists no registry selection snapshot and no ModePackRegistryUpdateSelected ledger event.
Distinct non-active registry candidates still select and replay with bounded ModePackSelectRegistryUpdateResult evidence.
No new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, inspection, preview, generic registry executor, automatic approval, or automatic activation is added.

Ledger and RPC outputs do not expose raw registry manifest, candidate JSON, provenance statement, signature, public key, prompt, provider response, file content, stdout/stderr, command, environment, paths, credentials, or secrets.
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test modepack_registry_update_selection_rejects_active_candidate_identity proves same-active denial before selection persistence.
Rust behavior test modepack_registry_update_selection_persists_bounded_candidate_and_replays preserves distinct-candidate selection and replay.
cargo check --workspace confirms the fix does not require protocol, store, or VSIX surface changes.
